mainTopic: How much intent is needed for יבום to take effect, and the Torah source that העראה counts as ביאה for all עריות
overview: The משנה taught that a יבם acquires his יבמה through ביאה whether by mistake or on purpose, by force or willingly. The גמרא looks for a real case of this. A sleeping man (רב יהודה) does not acquire her, and neither does one who fell from a roof (רבה). The case is a man who meant to be with his wife and his יבמה grabbed him. The source is the פסוק 'יבמה יבא עליה'. The גמרא shows that the other lessons drawn from that פסוק, the מצוה and כדרכה, come from other פסוקים. Then it studies רב יהודה's rule about a sleeping man, and explains that a dozing man (מתנמנם) does acquire. It also studies רבה's rule about the man who fell, and brings רבא's rule that intending any act of intercourse is enough. Finally, עולא learns from the פסוק about נדה that העראה counts by Torah law. The גמרא then searches for a source that covers the other עריות, testing pairs of sources. The discussion of רב אחא's objection continues on the next amud.

steps.title: A sleeping man does not acquire his יבמה
steps.stepSummary: This is the end of a quote from רב יהודה, used to reject the idea that the משנה's 'by mistake' case is a sleeping man.
steps.simpleTranslation: A man who was asleep has not acquired his יבמה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a challenge. It quotes רב יהודה to show that a sleeping man cannot be the משנה's case of acting 'by mistake.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says a יבם acquires his יבמה even by mistake. A sleeping man would be the most obvious mistake, but רב יהודה rules that a sleeping man does not acquire her at all. So the גמרא needs a different case.

keyTerms.meaning: Acquired, here meaning the יבום took effect
His יבמה, the widow of his brother who died without children

phrases.english: A sleeping man has not acquired his yevama.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the challenge against explaining the משנה's 'by mistake' case as a sleeping man.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that 'by mistake' in the משנה means a sleeping man.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב יהודה rules a sleeping man does not acquire, but the משנה says the one who acts by mistake does acquire.

steps.title: Maybe the case is a man who was accidentally inserted
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the משנה means a man who was pushed into the act by accident.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the משנה means a man who was accidentally inserted into her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a new picture of the משנה's case: a man who ended up in the act by accident, without planning it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since sleeping is ruled out, the גמרא tries a man who is awake but did not choose the act. This seems to fit 'by mistake' or 'by force.'

phrases.english: Rather, it refers to one who was inserted by accident.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a replacement case after the sleeping man was rejected.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The case is a sleeping man.
steps.terutzMaskana: The case is an awake man who was accidentally inserted.

steps.title: רבה says one who fell from a roof does not acquire
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the accident case using רבה's ruling about a man who fell from a roof.
steps.simpleTranslation: But רבה said: one who fell from a roof and was inserted pays four of the payments for damages, and if she was his יבמה, he has not acquired her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the new suggestion. רבה ruled that a man who falls and is inserted by accident does not acquire his יבמה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה's case is exactly an accidental insertion, and he says there is no acquisition. So the accident case also cannot be the משנה's case where the יבם does acquire.

keyTerms.meaning: Four of the five payments a damager owes
But didn't (so-and-so) say? Introduces a challenge

phrases.english: But didn't Rabba say:
One who fell from a roof and was inserted
is liable to pay four types of payment,
phrases.notes: A damager usually pays five things; here he skips the payment for shame, since he never meant to do it.

phrases.english: and with his yevama, he has not acquired her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the suggestion of step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that the משנה's case is an accidental insertion.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבה rules that an accidental insertion does not acquire the יבמה, which contradicts the משנה's ruling that he does acquire.

steps.title: He meant to be with his wife and his יבמה grabbed him
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא's final case: he intended to be with his wife, and his יבמה took hold of him.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is a case where he intended to be with his wife, and his יבמה grabbed him, and he lived with her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a new case that fits the משנה: the man was ready for the act with his wife in mind, but his יבמה forcefully took hold of him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here, unlike sleeping or falling, he did mean to do the act itself, just with a different woman. That is enough for the יבום to take effect, even though it happened by mistake and under force.

keyTerms.meaning: She took hold of him by force

steps.whatToRemember: A sleeping man or one who fell does not acquire his יבמה. A man who meant to be with his wife but was grabbed by his יבמה does acquire her.
steps.confusionAlert: 'By mistake' does not mean he had no intention for any act at all. He meant to do the act, just with his wife; that is different from sleeping or falling.

phrases.english: Rather, it is a case where he intended to be with his wife,
and his yevama grabbed hold of him, and he had relations with her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected case of step 2 with a workable one.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The case is an accidental insertion, which רבה says does not acquire.
steps.terutzMaskana: The case is one who intended the act with his wife and was grabbed by his יבמה.

steps.title: What is the case where both were forced?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how to picture the case from the school of רבי חייא where both the man and woman were forced.
steps.simpleTranslation: The case of 'both of them forced' from the school of רבי חייא: what does it look like?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for a picture of another case, taught in the school of רבי חייא, where both people were forced. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the last step only the man was forced; the יבמה acted on her own. Now the גמרא needs a case where neither one chose the act, yet it still works.

keyTerms.meaning: Of the school of רבי חייא
What is the case? How does it look?

phrases.english: The case of 'both of them forced' taught in the school of Rabbi Chiyya,
what are its circumstances?

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁנֵיהֶם אֲנוּסִים דְּבֵי רַבִּי חִיָּיא הֵיכִי דָּמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the case of step 4 and asks about a case where both sides were forced.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A realistic case where both the יבם and יבמה were forced.

steps.title: Non-Jews pushed them together
steps.stepSummary: The answer: he intended to be with his wife, and non-Jews grabbed him and pressed the two together.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a case where he intended to be with his wife, and non-Jews grabbed them and pressed them against each other, and he lived with her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question: outside people forced both of them together while he was ready for his wife.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Again he had intent for the act itself, just with his wife, so it is not like sleeping or falling. But now neither he nor the יבמה chose this; both were forced by others.

phrases.english: It is a case where he intended to be with his wife,
and non-Jews grabbed hold of him and pressed them against each other,
and he had relations with her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 5.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: He intended his wife, and non-Jews forced him and his יבמה together.

steps.title: Where do we learn this from?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source that יבום works even by mistake or by force.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know these rules?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now asks for the source in the תורה for the משנה's rule. This sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually we might expect an act of acquiring to need full intent. So the גמרא wants to know what teaches that יבום works no matter how it happened.

keyTerms.meaning: From where are these matters learned?

phrases.english: From where are these matters derived?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After defining the cases, the גמרא asks for their source.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The פסוק that teaches יבום works by mistake, on purpose, by force or willingly.

steps.title: The ברייתא learns it from 'יבמה יבא עליה'
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא reads the פסוק two ways: it teaches יבום is a מצוה, or alternatively that it works in every situation.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: 'Her brother-in-law shall come upon her' teaches it is a מצוה. Another explanation: 'Her brother-in-law shall come upon her' teaches it works whether by mistake or on purpose, whether forced or willingly.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא as the source. The ברייתא gives two readings of the same פסוק, and the second reading is the source for the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says simply that he 'comes upon her,' without any condition about intent. The second reading takes this to mean any act of being together counts, however it happened.

keyTerms.meaning: A command; here, the preferred choice over חליצה

phrases.english: As the Sages taught:
"Her brother-in-law shall come upon her": this is a מצוה.
phrases.notes: דברים 25:5

phrases.english: Another explanation: "Her brother-in-law shall come upon her":
whether by mistake or on purpose,
whether by force or willingly.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the source question of step 7.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ברייתא's second reading of 'יבמה יבא עליה' teaches that יבום works in every situation.

steps.title: But that פסוק was used for the מצוה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: the same פסוק was already used to teach that יבום is a מצוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't you already use it to teach that it is a מצוה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא's second reading. If the פסוק teaches the מצוה, how can it also teach that intent doesn't matter?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא presented two different readings of the same words. The challenge is that one phrase is already 'used up' by the first lesson, so it seems unavailable for the second one.

keyTerms.meaning: You took it out (used it) for

phrases.english: But didn't you use it to teach a מצוה?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the second reading in the ברייתא of step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: Using 'יבמה יבא עליה' to teach that יבום works in every situation.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same phrase already teaches that יבום is a מצוה, so it seems unavailable for a second lesson.

steps.title: The מצוה comes from a different פסוק
steps.stepSummary: The מצוה is learned from 'ואם לא יחפץ האיש,' so 'יבמה יבא עליה' is free to teach that יבום works in every situation.
steps.simpleTranslation: The מצוה is learned from 'And if the man does not wish': this implies that if he does wish, he does יבום. So when this פסוק comes, it teaches: whether by mistake or on purpose, whether forced or willingly.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. The מצוה of יבום has a different source, so our פסוק is free to teach the משנה's rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'And if the man does not wish' implies that if he does wish, he should do יבום, which is the מצוה. Since that lesson already comes from there, 'יבמה יבא עליה' is not needed for it. So it teaches that יבום works no matter how it happened.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And if the man does not wish'

steps.whatToRemember: The מצוה of יבום comes from 'ואם לא יחפץ האיש.' 'יבמה יבא עליה' teaches that יבום works by mistake or on purpose, by force or willingly.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for the משנה's rule. It also shows how the גמרא decides which פסוק is free to teach which lesson.

phrases.aramaic: לְמִצְוָה מִ״וְּאִם לֹא יַחְפּוֹץ הָאִישׁ״ נָפְקָא,
phrases.english: The מצוה is derived from "And if the man does not wish,"
phrases.notes: דברים 25:7

phrases.english: which implies: if he does wish, he performs levirate marriage,
and when this verse comes, it teaches:
phrases.notes: The verse is 'יבמה יבא עליה,' the פסוק from the ברייתא.

phrases.english: whether by mistake or on purpose,
whether by force or willingly.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְמִצְוָה מִוְּאִם לֹא יַחְפּוֹץ הָאִישׁ נָפְקָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 9.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Moving one lesson to a different פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'יבמה יבא עליה' is needed for the מצוה and can't teach anything else.
steps.terutzMaskana: The מצוה comes from 'ואם לא יחפץ האיש,' so 'יבמה יבא עליה' teaches that יבום works in every situation.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: יבום works whether by mistake or on purpose, by force or willingly, as learned from 'יבמה יבא עליה.'

steps.title: A second ברייתא reads each word of the יבום פסוק
steps.stepSummary: Another ברייתא learns from the words of the פסוק that יבום works through typical or atypical ביאה, that only ביאה completes it (not money or a document), and that it works even against her will. It also gives a second reading: it works even by mistake.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another ברייתא teaches: 'Her brother-in-law shall come upon her' means the typical way. 'And take her' means even not the typical way. 'And perform יבום' means ביאה completes the acquisition, but money and a document do not. 'And perform יבום with her' means even against her will. Another explanation: 'Her brother-in-law shall come upon her' means whether by mistake, etc.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second ברייתא that takes the יבום פסוק apart phrase by phrase, and each phrase teaches a separate rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each phrase gets its own job: the typical way, the atypical way, ביאה as the only thing that completes it, and the fact that it works against her will. The 'other explanation' at the end uses the first phrase for the rule from Step 8 instead: יבום works even by mistake. That double use sets up the question in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: The typical, normal way of intercourse
Money and a document, the other usual ways to marry a woman

phrases.english: It is taught in another ברייתא:
"Her brother-in-law shall come upon her": in the typical way.
phrases.notes: דברים 25:5

phrases.english: "And take her": even not in the typical way.
"And perform יבום": intercourse completes her acquisition,
but money and a document do not complete it.
"And perform יבום with her": even against her will.
Another explanation:
"Her brother-in-law shall come upon her": whether by mistake, etc.
phrases.notes: כו׳ means "etc." Finish it the way the ברייתא in Step 8 did: or on purpose, forced or willing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a second ברייתא with a fuller breakdown of the same פסוק discussed in Steps 8 to 10.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Each phrase of the יבום פסוק teaches its own rule. Alternatively, 'יבמה יבא עליה' teaches that יבום works whether done by mistake or on purpose.

steps.title: That phrase was already used for 'the typical way'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that 'יבמה יבא עליה' was already used to teach the typical way, so it cannot also teach that יבום works by mistake.
steps.simpleTranslation: But you already took that phrase to teach 'the typical way'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the 'other explanation': one phrase cannot be used for two different lessons.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first reading of the ברייתא, 'יבמה יבא עליה' taught כדרכה. If the 'other explanation' uses the same words for שוגג, where does כדרכה come from? The question is the same kind of objection as Step 9, now aimed at a different rule.

keyTerms.meaning: You already took it out (used it) for something else

phrases.english: But you already used it for "the typical way"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the 'other explanation' at the end of the ברייתא in Step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: The 'other explanation' that uses 'יבמה יבא עליה' for שוגג
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: One phrase cannot teach two separate rules, and this phrase was already used for כדרכה.

steps.title: 'The typical way' comes from a different פסוק
steps.stepSummary: כדרכה is learned from 'להקים לאחיו שם', meaning the place that can produce a child. So 'יבמה יבא עליה' is free to teach that יבום works by mistake or on purpose, forced or willing.
steps.simpleTranslation: That rule comes from 'to establish a name for his brother': it must be in the place where he can establish a name. So when this verse comes, it teaches: whether by mistake or on purpose, whether forced or willing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by moving the source for 'the typical way' to a different phrase, which frees up 'יבמה יבא עליה'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Establish a name' means having a child, and a child can only come from the typical way. So כדרכה is already covered. The phrase 'יבמה יבא עליה' is free to teach that the יבם's state of mind and willingness do not stop the יבום.

keyTerms.meaning: To establish a name for his brother, that is, to have a child in his name
It is learned from (literally, it comes out from)

steps.whatToRemember: כדרכה comes from 'להקים לאחיו שם', and 'יבמה יבא עליה' teaches that יבום works by mistake, on purpose, by force or willingly.

phrases.english: That rule is learned from "to establish a name for his brother",
phrases.notes: דברים 25:7

phrases.english: meaning in the place where he establishes a name.
So when this verse comes, it teaches:
whether by mistake or on purpose,
whether forced or willingly.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the objection of Step 12.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reassigning the source: the rule is learned from a different פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'יבמה יבא עליה' is needed to teach כדרכה.
steps.terutzMaskana: כדרכה comes from 'להקים לאחיו שם', so 'יבמה יבא עליה' teaches שוגג, מזיד, אונס and רצון.

steps.title: רב יהודה: a sleeping יבם does not acquire
steps.stepSummary: Going back to רב יהודה's statement, the גמרא quotes his rule that a sleeping יבם does not acquire his יבמה, because the פסוק requires him to intend an act of ביאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Back to the statement itself. רב יהודה said: a sleeping man has not acquired his יבמה, as the verse says 'her brother-in-law shall come upon her', meaning only when he intends her for the sake of ביאה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to look closely at רב יהודה's statement and quotes it in full.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יהודה reads 'יבא עליה' as needing a man who is aware that he is doing an act of ביאה. A sleeping man has no awareness at all, so nothing happens.

keyTerms.meaning: Back to the statement itself, to study it closely
For the sake of intercourse, knowing he is doing an act of ביאה

steps.confusionAlert: This does not contradict Step 13. A שוגג (like Step 4, who meant to be with his wife) still knows he is doing an act of ביאה. A sleeping man does not know anything.

phrases.english: Back to the statement itself:
Rav Yehuda said: a sleeping man
has not acquired his יבמה,
as the verse says: "Her brother-in-law shall come upon her",
meaning not until he intends her for the sake of intercourse.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new section, analyzing רב יהודה's statement on its own.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A sleeping יבם does not acquire his יבמה, because he must intend an act of ביאה.

steps.title: A ברייתא says awake or asleep both work
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב יהודה from a ברייתא that says יבום works whether awake or asleep.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it was taught: whether awake or asleep!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רב יהודה with a ברייתא that seems to say a sleeping person does acquire.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the ברייתא says asleep works, that directly opposes רב יהודה, who said a sleeping man does not acquire.

phrases.english: But it was taught: whether awake or asleep!
phrases.notes: The square bracket starts here and closes in Step 17. Those words are added in the corrected wording, so some versions don't have this back-and-forth.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב יהודה's rule in Step 14.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יהודה's rule that a sleeping man does not acquire
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא says יבום works even when asleep.

steps.title: Read it as talking about her
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא means the woman: whether she is awake or asleep.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say instead: whether she is awake or she is asleep.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by rereading the ברייתא so that it talks about the woman, not the man.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The woman's awareness is not needed for יבום, so she can be asleep. רב יהודה only requires the man's intent, so there is no contradiction.

keyTerms.meaning: Say instead, read it this way
She is awake / she is asleep

phrases.english: Say instead: whether she is awake or she is asleep.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 15.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the wording of the ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא means the man may be asleep.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא means the woman may be asleep.

steps.title: Another ברייתא names both him and her
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings another ברייתא that clearly says both he and she may be awake or asleep, so the rereading cannot work there.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it was taught: whether he is awake or he is asleep, whether she is awake or she is asleep!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב יהודה again, this time with a ברייתא that cannot be reread as talking about the woman alone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This ברייתא lists the man and the woman separately. So the answer of Step 16 fails, and a sleeping man seems to acquire.

keyTerms.meaning: He / she, making clear which person is meant

phrases.aramaic: וְהָתַנְיָא: בֵּין עֵר] הוּא בֵּין יָשֵׁן הוּא,
phrases.english: But it was taught: whether he is awake or he is asleep,

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין עֵרָה הִיא בֵּין יְשֵׁנָה הִיא!
phrases.english: whether she is awake or she is asleep!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָתַנְיָא בֵּין עֵר הוּא בֵּין יָשֵׁן הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows that the answer of Step 16 does not work for this ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יהודה's rule, together with the rereading in Step 16
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: This ברייתא names the man explicitly as asleep, so it cannot be reread as talking about her.

steps.title: The ברייתא means a man who is dozing
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that 'asleep' in that ברייתא means a man who is dozing, not fully asleep.
steps.simpleTranslation: What are we dealing with here? A man who is dozing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by narrowing the ברייתא's case: its 'asleep' is only half asleep.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A dozing man still has some awareness, so he counts as intending ביאה. רב יהודה was talking about someone fully asleep, so both can be true.

keyTerms.meaning: What case are we dealing with here? (introduces a narrower case)

phrases.english: What are we dealing with here?
With a man who is dozing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 17.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Asleep' in the ברייתא means fully asleep.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Asleep' means dozing, which still counts as having intent.

steps.title: What counts as dozing?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for a definition of מתנמנם.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the case of dozing?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks exactly what state counts as 'dozing', which sets up רב אשי's definition in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the whole answer depends on dozing being different from sleeping, the גמרא needs a clear line between them.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the case? What does it look like?

phrases.english: What is the case of dozing?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for a definition of the term used in Step 18.

steps.title: רב אשי defines dozing
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי says a dozing person is half asleep and half awake: he answers when called but cannot give a sensible reply, and when reminded later, he remembers.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: asleep but not asleep, awake but not awake. For example, they call him and he answers, but he cannot give a sensible reply, and when they remind him later, he remembers.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי gives a practical test for when someone counts as dozing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The sign is that he responds and later remembers, which shows some awareness was there. That small awareness is enough to count as intending ביאה, unlike someone fully asleep.

keyTerms.meaning: To give back a sensible answer

steps.whatToRemember: A fully sleeping יבם does not acquire (רב יהודה). A dozing one does: he answers when called but not sensibly, and remembers when reminded.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
asleep but not asleep,
awake but not awake,
for example, when they call him he answers,
but he cannot give a sensible reply,
and when they remind him, he remembers.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי נִים וְלָא נִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 19.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Dozing means half asleep: he answers when called but not sensibly, and remembers when reminded.

steps.title: Falling from a roof: four payments, no acquisition
steps.stepSummary: רבה rules that a man who fell from a roof and was inserted into a woman pays נזק, צער, שבת, and ריפוי, but not בושת. If she is his יבמה, he does not acquire her.
steps.simpleTranslation: The statement itself: רבה said: if a man fell from a roof and was inserted into a woman, he must pay four things, and if she is his יבמה he has not acquired her. The four are injury, pain, lost work, and medical costs. He does not pay for shame, because a person only pays for shame if he meant to do the act.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to a statement of רבה it quoted earlier and now studies it directly. It also spells out which payments he owes and why בושת is left out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The fall was a pure accident, but damage payments like נזק, צער, שבת, and ריפוי apply even without intent. בושת needs intent, so it drops out. For the same reason, an unintended act does not count as the ביאה that acquires a יבמה.

keyTerms.meaning: The matter itself: the גמרא goes back to analyze a statement it quoted earlier
Acquired the יבמה as his wife

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the basic rule that acquiring a יבמה through ביאה requires some intent, which רבא develops in the next step.

phrases.english: The matter itself: Rabba said:
phrases.notes: Literally 'the body.' The גמרא is going back to look closely at a statement it brought earlier.

phrases.english: If one fell from a roof and was inserted
he is liable for four things,
phrases.notes: These are four of the five payments someone owes for hurting another person.

phrases.english: and with his yevama, he has not acquired her.
For injury, pain, loss of work, and medical costs.
But for shame he is not liable,
as the Master said:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין חַיָּיב עַל הַבּוֹשֶׁת עַד שֶׁיִּתְכַּוֵּון.
phrases.english: One is not liable for shame unless he intends.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the discussion of מתנמנם and returns to analyze רבה's statement on its own.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An accidental insertion makes him owe נזק, צער, שבת, and ריפוי, but not בושת, and it does not acquire a יבמה.

steps.title: Intending a wall versus intending an animal
steps.stepSummary: רבא rules that if a man meant to press against a wall and instead entered his יבמה, he does not acquire her. If he meant an animal and instead entered his יבמה, he does acquire her, since he intended some act of intercourse.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: if he meant to press into a wall and pressed into his יבמה, he has not acquired her. If he meant to press into an animal and pressed into his יבמה, he has acquired her, because he did intend some act of intercourse.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא adds a sharper rule about how much intent is needed for ביאה with a יבמה to count.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He does not have to intend this specific woman or a permitted act. It is enough that he intended an act of intercourse of some kind. A wall is not intercourse at all, so it is like the man who fell from the roof.

keyTerms.meaning: For the purpose of intercourse in general (any intercourse)

steps.confusionAlert: רבא is not saying the man had a proper intent for יבום. He only needs to have intended an act of intercourse of any kind, even a forbidden one.
steps.whatToRemember: Acquiring a יבמה through ביאה needs only general intent for intercourse. A pure accident (falling) or a non-sexual act (a wall) does not acquire her.

phrases.english: Rava said:
If he intended to press into a wall
and he pressed into his yevama, he has not acquired her.
If he intended to press into an animal
and he pressed into the yevama, he has acquired her,
since he did intend some act of intercourse in general.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on רבה's rule by defining what kind of intent is enough for acquisition.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: General intent for any intercourse is enough to acquire a יבמה. Intending a non-sexual act is not.

steps.title: Source in the תורה that העראה counts
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's words אחד המערה. עולא derives from a פסוק about נדה that העראה counts as intercourse by Torah law.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said 'both one who begins the act.' עולא said: how do we know from the Torah that העראה counts? The פסוק says: 'And a man who lies with a woman in her sickness and uncovers her nakedness, he has made naked (הערה) her fountain.' From here we learn that העראה counts by Torah law.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic from the משנה. עולא gives the Torah source that even the first stage of intercourse counts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק uses the word הערה, the same root as העראה. This shows that the Torah treats the first stage of intercourse with a נדה as a full forbidden act.

keyTerms.meaning: One who only begins the act of intercourse
A woman in her sickness (a נדה)

phrases.english: Both one who begins the act.
phrases.notes: These words are quoted from our משנה, which says both the one who begins and the one who finishes have acquired the יבמה.

phrases.english: Ulla said:
From where do we know that the first stage of intercourse counts by Torah law?

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״וְאִישׁ אֲשֶׁר יִשְׁכַּב אֶת אִשָּׁה דָּוָה
phrases.english: As it says: 'And a man who lies with a woman in her sickness
phrases.notes: ויקרא 20:18

phrases.english: and uncovers her nakedness,
he has made naked her fountain,'
phrases.notes: The word הערה has the same root as העראה, which is where the proof comes from.

phrases.english: From here we learn that the first stage counts by Torah law.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶחָד הַמְעָרֶה. אָמַר עוּלָּא: מִנַּיִן לְהַעֲרָאָה מִן הַתּוֹרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new topic. The גמרא moves on to the next phrase of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The first stage of intercourse counts as intercourse by Torah law, learned from the word הערה in the פסוק about נדה.

steps.title: What about the other forbidden relations?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: the פסוק only teaches העראה for נדה, so where do we learn it for the other עריות?
steps.simpleTranslation: We found a source for נדה. From where do we know it for the other forbidden relations?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that עולא's פסוק only speaks about נדה and asks for a source covering all other עריות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: עולא's proof is limited to the case the פסוק is talking about. The גמרא wants to know whether העראה counts for every ערוה, not only נדה.

phrases.english: We have found it for a menstruating woman;
from where do we know it for the other forbidden relations?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how far עולא's source reaches.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A Torah source that העראה counts for all עריות, not just נדה.

steps.title: Why we cannot simply learn from נדה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects learning the other עריות from נדה, because נדה has a unique stringency: she makes the man who has relations with her טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say we should learn from נדה, that does not work. נדה is more severe, since she makes the man who has relations with her טמא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא suggests an easy answer to its own question, learning everything from נדה, and then knocks it down. This sets up the search for a better source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a מה לנדה argument. A rule from a stricter case cannot be applied to milder cases. Since נדה has an extra stringency, maybe העראה counts only for her.

keyTerms.meaning: What about X, which has a special feature: a formula used to block a comparison
Makes the man who has relations with her ritually impure

phrases.english: And if you say: let us learn it from a menstruating woman,
what about a menstruating woman?
She makes the one who has relations with her impure!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא: נֵילַף מִנִּדָּה, מָה לְנִדָּה שֶׁכֵּן מְטַמְּאָה אֶת בּוֹעֲלָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Blocks the obvious answer to the question just asked.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea of learning העראה for all עריות from נדה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: נדה is stricter because she makes the man טמא, so a rule about her cannot be extended to milder עריות.

steps.title: Trying to learn from a brother's wife
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests learning העראה for the other עריות from אשת אח. The Torah calls her 'נדה', which compares her to a נדה, where העראה already counts.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, learn it from a brother's wife. The Torah says: 'A man who takes his brother's wife, it is נדה.' Is a brother's wife always a נדה? No. It means she is like a נדה. Just as with נדה העראה counts, so too with a brother's wife העראה counts.
steps.whatsHappening: After learning from נדה failed, the גמרא tries a new source: אשת אח, whom the Torah links to נדה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק calls a brother's wife 'נדה', even though she is obviously not always a נדה. So the word must be a comparison: she has the same rules as נדה, including that העראה counts. Because אשת אח does not have נדה's special strictness of making the man טמא, she might serve as a better model for the other עריות.

keyTerms.meaning: A brother's wife, who is forbidden to a man
It comes from (it is learned from)
Like a נדה; treated with the same rules

phrases.english: Rather, it comes from a brother's wife,

phrases.aramaic: דִּכְתִיב: ״וְאִישׁ אֲשֶׁר יִקַּח אֶת אֵשֶׁת אָחִיו
phrases.english: as it is written: "And a man who takes his brother's wife,
it is נדה"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 20:21

phrases.english: Is his brother's wife always a נדה?
phrases.notes: The word in square brackets, 'always', is added in the corrected wording.

phrases.english: Rather, it means she is like a נדה:
just as with a נדה, העראה counts,
so too with a brother's wife, העראה counts.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a new source after learning from נדה was rejected.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Learn העראה for the other עריות from אשת אח, who is compared to נדה.

steps.title: A brother's wife is special: the number of forbidden women can grow
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects learning from אשת אח. Her prohibition has a special strictness: the brother can keep marrying more women, and every one of them becomes forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: What about a brother's wife? She is special, because it is in his power to add more. If the brother wants, he can keep betrothing women, even a thousand, and each one becomes forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down the אשת אח source by pointing out something unique about her.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With most עריות, the number of forbidden women is fixed by family. With אשת אח, the brother can keep creating new forbidden women just by betrothing them. That extra stretch makes this prohibition 'stronger', so it cannot teach about the other עריות.

keyTerms.meaning: It is in his power to increase (the number of forbidden women)

phrases.english: What about a brother's wife?
She is special, because it is in his power to add more,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאִי בָּעֵי מְקַדֵּשׁ וְאָזֵיל כִּי אַלְפָּא.
phrases.english: for if he wants, he can keep on betrothing, up to a thousand.
phrases.notes: 'He' is the brother. Every woman he betroths becomes forbidden to this man.

steps.triggerLanguage: מָה לְאֵשֶׁת אָח שֶׁכֵּן בְּיָדוֹ לְרַבּוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the source offered in step 26.
steps.kashyaTarget: Learning the other עריות from אשת אח
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: אשת אח has a unique strictness: the brother can keep adding forbidden women. So she cannot be a model for the other עריות.

steps.title: Trying to learn from a father's sister and a mother's sister
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests learning from אחות אב and אחות אם, because their פסוק uses the word 'הערה'.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, learn it from a father's sister and a mother's sister. The Torah says: 'Do not uncover the nakedness of your mother's sister or your father's sister, for he has made his relative bare (הערה).'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries a third source: the פסוק about aunts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'הערה' in this פסוק comes from the same root as העראה. So the פסוק itself seems to say that even the first stage of intercourse counts with an aunt. If so, maybe we can spread this rule to the other עריות.

keyTerms.meaning: Made bare; the same root as העראה

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אָתְיָא מֵאֲחוֹת אָב וַאֲחוֹת אֵם,
phrases.english: Rather, it comes from a father's sister and a mother's sister,

phrases.aramaic: דִּכְתִיב: ״וְעֶרְוַת אֲחוֹת אִמְּךָ וַאֲחוֹת אָבִיךָ לֹא תְגַלֵּה
phrases.english: as it is written: "And the nakedness of your mother's sister and your father's sister you shall not uncover,
for he has made his relative bare."
phrases.notes: ויקרא 20:19. The word הערה sounds like העראה, and that is the point of quoting it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָתְיָא מֵאֲחוֹת אָב וַאֲחוֹת אֵם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers another source after אשת אח was rejected.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Learn העראה from the aunts, whose פסוק uses the word הערה.

steps.title: Aunts are special: their prohibition comes on its own
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects learning from the aunts. Their prohibition is 'איסור הבא מאליו': it comes from birth, not from anyone's marriage.
steps.simpleTranslation: This can be challenged: what about a father's sister and a mother's sister? They are special, because their prohibition comes on its own.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down the aunts source by showing a way they are unique.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An aunt is forbidden just because of who she was born as. No marriage is needed to create the prohibition. Many other עריות become forbidden only through a marriage, so a prohibition that comes on its own counts as stronger and cannot teach about them.

keyTerms.meaning: A prohibition that comes on its own, without any act like marriage

phrases.english: This can be challenged:
What about a father's sister and a mother's sister?
They are special, because theirs is a prohibition that comes on its own.
phrases.notes: She is forbidden from birth, simply because she is his parent's sister. Nobody's marriage made her forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא לְמִיפְרַךְ מָה לַאֲחוֹת אָב וַאֲחוֹת אֵם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the source offered in step 28.
steps.kashyaTarget: Learning the other עריות from the aunts
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The aunts' prohibition comes on its own from birth, which is a unique strictness. So they cannot be a model for the other עריות.

steps.title: New plan: learn from two sources together
steps.stepSummary: Since no single source works, the גמרא suggests combining two sources to learn the rule for the others.
steps.simpleTranslation: It cannot come from one source alone. So let it come from two together.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא changes strategy. This line sets up the next move: picking which two sources to combine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each single source was rejected because of its own special strictness. If we use two sources that have different strictnesses, neither special feature can be the reason for the rule. That leaves העראה as a shared rule we can apply to the others.

keyTerms.meaning: Let it come (let us learn it)

phrases.english: From one source it cannot come;
let it come, one case from two.
phrases.notes: The word in square brackets, 'one', is added in the corrected wording. The idea is to learn each other ערוה from these two sources together.

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵחֲדָא לָא אָתְיָא תֵּיתֵי חֲדָא מִתַּרְתֵּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After every single source was rejected, the גמרא proposes combining sources.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Learn the rule by combining two sources.

steps.title: Which two sources should we combine?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which pair of sources to use.
steps.simpleTranslation: From which ones should it come?
steps.whatsHappening: A short question that sets up the next move: testing different pairs of sources.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are three sources: נדה, אשת אח, and the aunts. Each pair has to be checked, to make sure the two don't share a strictness that the other עריות lack.

phrases.english: From which ones should it come?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how to carry out the plan from step 30.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which pair of sources can teach העראה for the other עריות?

steps.title: Trying the pair: brother's wife plus the aunts
steps.stepSummary: The first pair the גמרא tests is אשת אח together with אחות אב and אחות אם.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let it come from a brother's wife and from a father's sister and a mother's sister.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests its first pair of sources. The very next line checks whether this pair works.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אשת אח's weakness was that the brother can add more forbidden women. The aunts' weakness was that their prohibition comes on its own. These two weaknesses are different, so together they might seem to cancel each other out.

phrases.aramaic: תֵּיתֵי מֵאֵשֶׁת אָח וַאֲחוֹת אָב וַאֲחוֹת אֵם
phrases.english: Let it come from a brother's wife and a father's sister and a mother's sister.

steps.triggerLanguage: תֵּיתֵי מֵאֵשֶׁת אָח וַאֲחוֹת אָב וַאֲחוֹת אֵם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the first possible answer to step 31's question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Combine אשת אח with the aunts.

steps.title: That pair fails: both are forbidden as family
steps.stepSummary: The pair of אשת אח and the aunts is rejected. Both are forbidden because of family closeness (שאר), and not all עריות are like that.
steps.simpleTranslation: What about these? They are special, because they are forbidden as family.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the pair it just suggested, by finding something both cases share.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Combining two sources only works if the two don't share a special feature. אשת אח and the aunts both share one: they are forbidden as relatives (שאר). So the rule might come from that family closeness, and they cannot teach about an ערוה that is not forbidden for that reason.

phrases.english: What about these?
They are special, because they are forbidden as family relatives.

steps.triggerLanguage: מָה לְהָנָךְ שֶׁכֵּן אֲסוּרִין מִשּׁוּם שְׁאֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the pair proposed in step 32.
steps.kashyaTarget: Combining אשת אח with the aunts
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Both sources share a common strictness: they are forbidden as family (שאר). So together they cannot teach about עריות that lack it.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows the rule for learning from two sources: the pair must not share a special strictness. The גמרא will need a different pair.

steps.title: Trying a new pair: the נדה and the aunts
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests learning the rule from נדה combined with אחות אב and אחות אם.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, let us learn it from נדה together with a father's sister and a mother's sister.
steps.whatsHappening: The first pair failed, so the גמרא offers a new pair: נדה plus the aunts. The next line will test this pair.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The last pair failed because both were forbidden through family closeness (שאר). נדה is not a family relative, so pairing her with the aunts seems to fix that problem.

keyTerms.meaning: Let it come; let us learn it from
A woman forbidden because of her menstrual period

phrases.english: Rather, let it come from נדה
and a father's sister and a mother's sister.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא תֵּיתֵי מִנִּדָּה וַאֲחוֹת אָב וַאֲחוֹת אֵם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected pair from step 33 with a new pair.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Learn from נדה together with the aunts.

steps.title: Rejected: both are forbidden on their own
steps.stepSummary: The pair of נדה and the aunts fails, because both are an איסור הבא מאליו and not created through marriage.
steps.simpleTranslation: What about these? They are a prohibition that comes on its own.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down the pair of נדה and the aunts. Both share a feature that אשת איש does not have.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The aunts are forbidden from birth, and נדה becomes forbidden by her own body. No marriage creates either איסור. So they cannot teach about עריות that do come from a marriage.

keyTerms.meaning: What about these? (a way of saying these cases are special)
Since; because they have this special feature
A prohibition that comes on its own, not through any marriage

phrases.english: What about these
that they are a prohibition that comes on its own.
phrases.notes: This is the same weakness the גמרא used against the aunts in step 29.

steps.triggerLanguage: מָה לְהָנָךְ שֶׁכֵּן אִיסּוּר הַבָּא מֵאֵלָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the pair proposed in step 34.
steps.kashyaTarget: The pair of נדה and the aunts
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Both sources share a stringent feature (איסור הבא מאליו), so their shared rule may not extend to עריות created by marriage.

steps.title: A pair with no weakness: נדה and אשת אח
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא proposes learning from נדה and אשת אח, and claims nothing can be said against this pair.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, let us learn it from נדה and a brother's wife, for what objection can you raise?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא suggests a new pair, נדה and אשת אח, and challenges anyone to find a problem with it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This pair fixes both earlier problems. נדה is not a relative, so the pair is not all about שאר. אשת אח becomes forbidden through a marriage, so the pair is not all איסור הבא מאליו.

keyTerms.meaning: For what objection can you raise? (there is no weakness)

phrases.english: Rather, let it come from נדה and a brother's wife,
for what can you refute?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא תֵּיתֵי מִנִּדָּה וְאֵשֶׁת אָח דְּמַאי פָּרְכַתְּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a new pair that avoids the weaknesses raised in steps 33 and 35.
steps.whyThisMatters: This pair is built to escape both earlier objections. It shows how a צד השוה must avoid any stringency the two sources share.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Learn from נדה together with אשת אח, which share no special stringency.

steps.title: רב אחא's objection: אשת איש can become permitted
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בריה דרב איקא argues that נדה and אשת אח cannot become permitted while the cause of their איסור still exists, but אשת איש can.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא son of רב איקא objects: What about נדה and a brother's wife? They have no permission while the one who forbids them is still there. Can you say the same about a married woman, who can become permitted while the one who forbids her is still alive?
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחא finds a weakness after all: the new pair shares a stringency that אשת איש does not have.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A נדה stays forbidden as long as her period lasts, and a brother's wife stays forbidden as long as the brother is alive. A married woman can become permitted while her husband is still alive, through a divorce. So the rule might not carry over to אשת איש.

keyTerms.meaning: While the one (or thing) that forbids them still exists
Can you say? (can you apply the same rule?)

phrases.aramaic: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִיקָא:
phrases.english: Rav Acha son of Rav Ika strongly objects to it:
What about a נדה and a brother's wife,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁכֵּן אֵין לָהֶם הֶיתֵּר בְּחַיֵּי אוֹסְרָן,
phrases.english: since they have no permission during the life of what forbids them,
phrases.notes: For a נדה, what forbids her is her flow of blood. For a brother's wife, it is the brother himself.

phrases.english: can you say this about a married woman,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁכֵּן יֵשׁ לָהּ הֶיתֵּר בְּחַיֵּי אוֹסְרָהּ!
phrases.english: who has permission during the life of the one who forbids her!
phrases.notes: Her husband can divorce her while he is alive, and then she is permitted to others.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִיקָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge 'דמאי פרכת' from step 36 by naming a shared weakness.
steps.kashyaTarget: The pair of נדה and אשת אח
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Both sources cannot become permitted while the cause of their איסור exists, but אשת איש can, so the rule may not carry over to her.

steps.title: רב אחא מדפתי pushes back: are they permitted afterward?
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא מדפתי questions the objection. He asks whether נדה and אשת אח really become permitted once the cause of their איסור is gone, and he begins with נדה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא of דפתי said to רבינא: Is that to say that only while the forbidding cause exists do נדה and a brother's wife have no permission, but afterward they do have permission? A נדה —
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחא מדפתי challenges the objection from the last step. He starts to show that the comparison does not really work, beginning with נדה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The objection treated נדה and אשת אח as cases that wait for the cause to end and then become permitted. רב אחא מדפתי questions that picture, and he is about to explain the case of נדה.

keyTerms.meaning: Is that to say? (introduces a doubtful assumption)

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַחָא מִדִּפְתִּי לְרָבִינָא:
phrases.english: Rav Acha of Difti said to Ravina:
Is that to say that a נדה and a brother's wife

phrases.aramaic: בְּחַיֵּי אוֹסְרָן הוּא דְּאֵין לָהֶם הֶיתֵּר,
phrases.english: have no permission only during the life of what forbids them,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל לְאַחַר מִכָּאן יֵשׁ לָהֶם הֶיתֵּר?
phrases.english: but afterward they do have permission?
A נדה —

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַחָא מִדִּפְתִּי לְרָבִינָא אַטּוּ נִדָּה וְאֵשֶׁת אָח
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the assumption behind רב אחא בריה דרב איקא's objection in step 37.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The objection from step 37 against the pair of נדה and אשת אח
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It assumes נדה and אשת אח become permitted once the cause of their איסור ends. That assumption is being questioned, and the explanation continues with נדה.
